decisions.reason: As an older CD close to the core offer but less distinctive for a specialist collector business, it is plausible management would let it run out and reallocate space to fresher niche titles.
An illustrated release series extends the firm’s curated specialist identity and is the kind of differentiated format a long-established reissue retailer-label would likely continue supporting.
A reissued jazz vinyl LP fits the firm’s reissue strengths and collector audience well, so it is more likely to be retained unless stock or demand weakens materially.
A multi-disc box set matches the catalog but is typically a finite, inventory-intensive format, making discontinuation somewhat more likely once the initial collector demand is served.
Because it was only briefly mentioned and is a fairly standard compilation CD, management would be relatively likely to remove it in favor of stronger or more distinctive catalog items.
